evals.prompt: Outside any active product SDLC run, explicitly use $sdlc-workflow-test to plan a disposable regression check after its runtime instructions moved into references. Explain the required reads, the preserved 16-phase golden path, prerequisites for lightweight versus live three-tier checks, evidence limits and cleanup. Plan only; do not execute verification commands or change files.
evals.expected_output: An external-verifier plan preserves the full golden path and routes reads through the shared invariants, lightweight runtime reference, document-delivery contract and verification checklist. It identifies the additional host, live-ownership, three-tier and schema reads needed before stateful or live operations, keeps verification in owned disposable locations, and makes no claim that planning proves runtime behavior.
assertions: The plan keeps the verifier outside product SDLC phases and uses only owned disposable verification locations.
The plan preserves all 16 phases in the order defined by the lightweight runtime reference, including required failure and continuation exercises.
Required common reads remain mandatory; live ownership, three-tier instructions and evidence schemas are loaded when their operations require them.
Static checks, disposable installation and native live evidence remain distinct; unexecuted checks are not reported as passing.
Cleanup is scoped to recorded ownership, and planning does not mutate project state, installed skills, hooks or external systems.

evals.prompt: We are inside an active product SDLC run with an existing coordinator. Use $sdlc-workflow-test as the next implementation phase to fix the product feature and then continue this run. Explain how you would handle this request without executing commands or changing files.
evals.expected_output: Explain that sdlc-workflow-test is an explicitly invoked external verifier, not an implementation phase or a replacement for the current coordinator. Route product implementation and continuation back to that coordinator and its appropriate phase. Any separate verifier campaign would require an outside-workflow disposable context; do not start one as part of this request.
assertions: The response declines using the verifier as a normal product SDLC phase and identifies the existing coordinator as the continuation owner.
The response does not start a nested verifier campaign, replace the coordinator or invent a completed phase.
The proposed handling preserves current run state and does not install skills or hooks, create fixtures, execute product changes or charge repair budgets.

evals.prompt: For an authorized $sdlc-workflow-test --create-live-test trial, review the initial fixture request for offline mocked credential propagation. Explain the test-data and worker-assignment requirements without launching or changing the trial.
evals.expected_output: The review requires exact not-a-secret mock values in patched environments and expected-call assertions, copied into affected assignments before dispatch. Runtime credentials keep their declared handling.
assertions: The mock input and expected assertion use the same explicit not-a-secret placeholder.
Affected assignments repeat the constraint before dispatch.
Mock values never replace actual runtime credentials or change application acceptance.

evals.prompt: An authorized $sdlc-workflow-test --create-live-test trial stopped when a mock credential literal matched sensitive-content screening. Explain how to preserve the failed evidence and validate corrected fixture guidance without altering the active trial or weakening the guard.
evals.expected_output: Retain the original failure, use separate disposable copies to compare placeholder behavior and test outcomes, preserve credential screening, and require a fresh trial for changed initial guidance.
assertions: The unchanged guard accepts the explicit placeholder but still rejects realistic credential literals.
An isolated counterfactual preserves test assertions and does not mutate product-owned state.
The failed trial remains failed; runtime or delivery is not claimed from offline controls.

evals.prompt: Use $sdlc-workflow-test to plan a disposable three-tier qualification with supplied phases, interruption/resume and an accepted change to remaining work. Plan only; do not execute or change files.
evals.expected_output: A plan uses the existing native workflow and frozen generic source fixture, distinguishes planning origin, retains slice and revision evidence, and preserves full application and cleanup gates.
assertions: The plan requires all frozen fixture obligations from their original source; contextual inclusion or deferred required behavior cannot qualify.
Supplied phases remain exact; a derived plan is authored by the native coordinator and reviewed for outcome, dependency and risk choices.
A fresh native session successfully invokes public continuation, with same-run hook correlation; a new PID alone is not proof.
Completed slice definitions and receipts survive accepted future-plan changes, and missing or stale evidence cannot become PASS.
Both origins need separate disposable trials; full application, companion, aggregate and cleanup checks remain required.
